paragraphs.text: McMurtry et al. (1992) studied 46 members of a large 5-generation kindred with familial benign hypocalciuric hypercalcemia (FBH) and found 19 of them affected. In the 15 hypercalcemic members examined biochemically, serum immunoreactive PTH, measured in 3 separate immunoassays, became supranormal by about age 30 years and appeared to rise further after that. Serum alkaline phosphatase activity and creatinine were normal, but inorganic phosphate levels were lower than in unaffected members of the kindred. Radiographs of 3 of 5 affected adults older than 40 years showed changes suggestive of osteomalacia. In one of them, a 51-year-old woman, iliac crest biopsy confirmed defective skeletal mineralization. McMurtry et al. (1992) concluded that the disorder in this kindred may not be totally benign, because osteomalacia, perhaps due to mild hypophosphatemia, can develop in adulthood. They raised the possibility that they had observed an unusual variant of FBH.

paragraphs.text: Hannan et al. (2010) typed 24 polymorphic loci in the Oklahoma kindred and found that the disorder segregated with a chromosome 19q13 haplotype, with a peak lod score of 6.92 at zero recombination with D19S606. Recombinants in individuals II.2, III.3, and III.4 refined the FBHH3 locus to a 4.1-Mb interval flanked by D19S112 and rs245111. This interval contains 135 protein-coding genes and 24 predicted genes. The syntenic region on mouse chromosome 7 contains 4 Casr-related sequences (Gprc2a-rs) that have no human homologs. Comparative analysis showed that 2 conserved segments were inverted and that an 11.6-Mb region containing 35 murine genes, including the 4 Gprc2a-rs genes, is absent from the human genome. FBHH3 therefore cannot be attributed to these genes.

The authors then sequenced AP2S1 in 50 unrelated FHH patients without CASR mutations. They found 11 heterozygous missense mutations, all affecting arg15: 4 R15C, 3 arg15-to-his (R15H), and 4 arg15-to-leu (R15L). In HEK293 cells stably expressing CaSR, all 3 arg15 mutants shifted the concentration-response curve to the right, with a significantly higher EC50 than wildtype, indicating reduced sensitivity to extracellular calcium. With the cys15 mutant, the EC50 was higher than with vector alone, suggesting a possible dominant-negative effect.
